Design: uncaught throw of {code:'E300',message:'Error: ...'} yields clean exit-1 with no traceback (verified no stack dumps on bad ids, bad JSON, missing files, unknown commands). Env vars read via env() wrapped in try/catch for the E302-unset case (unset/empty TASKMAN_CMD -> help). db.exec bind args kept all-Text per STDLIB ([Text]?), relying on SQLite INTEGER affinity for WHERE id = ?. trials.notes: Verifier passes 27/27 on the AOT binary at workdir/taskman (source: taskman.misa). Key design decisions: exit code 1 via print('Error: ...') + uncaught throw (AOT exits 1 with a one-line 'line:col: CODE: msg' report on stderr — no traceback); env-var defaults via try/catch around env() (E302); id validation by manual digit scan (str.ord/str.slice) rather than int() to reject '0', '-3', ' 5', 'abc'; SQL injection avoided by binding titles with '?' placeholders while interpolating only validated-int ids and fixed status literals; import validates array-ness by checking the trimmed text starts with '[' then json.parse in try/catch (parse errors can't be distinguished from field-access errors otherwise); bad-status import items produce 'Error: bad status'. Edge cases verified manually beyond the verifier: bad ids, 23-digit ids (no task #<raw>), injection title stored literally, non-array JSON, empty array import, unknown command prints error + usage with exit 1. Hardest parts were Misa-specific: the '{{'/'}}' interpolation trap and the missing else-if. Typed 'table tasks' + db.query gave compile-time column checking for free.

trials.notes: Single-file taskman.misa (~190 lines), AOT-compiled to ./taskman; verifier run twice for stability, both RESULT: PASS 27/27. Key techniques: table decl for typed db.query; try/catch around env() for unset vars (E302); Text-only SQL binds with digit-validated id interpolation into SQL; json.stringify prefix check to reject non-array imports; dot access (not string indexing) on dynamic records; uncaught throw of an Error record for exit-1 user errors after printing the clean 'Error: ...' line. Extra edge cases probed manually (unset cmd, empty/negative ids, quoted titles, bad-status/missing-title/non-array/empty-array imports) all behave per spec with no tracebacks. Hardest part was discovering that string-indexing dynamic records never works (my first probe misread the E300 as 'missing key'). What helped: small interpreter probes of each dynamic behavior before writing the full program, then verifying each on AOT since several behaviors differ subtly.
